title: Reading practice: The Shadow Puppet Show
description: A short story about two friends and a puppet show, plus a school schedule: sequence, feelings, cause and effect, and reading a table.

stimuli.title: The Shadow Puppet Show
paragraphs: Kiran and Tomás had one week to make a shadow puppet show for their class. Kiran cut a bird from black cardboard, and Tomás taped it to a long stick. On Monday, they set a lamp and a white sheet in the hallway and tried their bird for the first time.

The shadow on the sheet looked like a gray blob. The edges were blurry, and the bird was tiny. Kiran’s stomach felt tight. “Nobody will know it is a bird,” she whispered. Tomás shrugged. “Maybe we should just draw a picture instead,” he said.

Kiran did not want to give up. When Ms. Okafor walked by, Kiran raised her hand. “Excuse me, could you help us?” she asked. “Our shadow does not look right.” Ms. Okafor did not take the stick. Instead, she asked two questions. “Where is your bird? How far is it from the sheet?” Then she pointed at the lamp and said, “Try a different place and see what changes.”

Tomás carried the bird closer to the sheet. At once, the edges of the shadow became sharp. “I can see its wings!” Kiran said. Then Kiran moved the lamp closer to the bird, and the shadow grew bigger and filled the sheet. They kept testing until the bird looked just right.

On Friday, the class sat in the dark. Kiran’s hands shook as the bird began to fly across the sheet. Then she heard the class gasp. Her stomach felt light. When the show ended, everyone clapped, and Ms. Okafor gave her a thumbs up. Kiran smiled at Tomás. “I am glad we did not give up,” she said.

stimuli.title: Reading Buddies Visit: Friday Plan
stimuli.caption: A morning schedule for the day when second graders visit Room 6 as reading buddies.
rows: Meet your buddy and choose a book
Share a drawing with the class
Walk your buddy back to class

items.stem: Put the story events in the order they happened.

items.text: Kiran asked Ms. Okafor for help.
The class gasped when the bird flew across the sheet.
Kiran and Tomás saw a blurry gray blob on the sheet.
Tomás carried the bird closer to the sheet.

items.explanation: The shadow looked like a blob first. Kiran then asked for help, Tomás moved the bird, and at the show the class gasped.

support.clue: Look for time clues in the paragraphs: “On Monday,” “At once,” and “On Friday.” Ask which event could not happen until another one was finished.
support.frame: At first, ______. Then, ______. After that, ______. At the end, ______.
support.model:
Mentor example (a different story). Leo loses his mitten on the way to school. He looks under the bench, then asks the bus driver, and last he finds it in his backpack. The order is: lose it, look for it, ask for help, find it.

Now put the events of your story in time order the same way.

items.stem: Which sentence best explains why Kiran’s feelings changed between Monday’s practice and Friday’s show?

options.text: She decided her bird was not good enough, so she stopped caring about the show at all.
She tested new places for the bird and the lamp until the shadow looked right, so she felt glad.
Tomás made all of the changes by himself, so she had nothing left to worry about at the show.
Ms. Okafor fixed the puppet for them, so the shadow looked right without more testing.

distractors.a: Kiran does not stop caring; at the end she says she is glad they did not give up.
distractors.c: Both children made changes: Tomás moved the bird and Kiran moved the lamp.
distractors.d: The story says Ms. Okafor did not take the stick; she only asked questions and gave a hint.

items.explanation: Kiran and Tomás tested new places for the bird and the lamp until the shadow looked right, so Kiran felt glad at the Friday show instead of worried.

support.clue: Reread the last two paragraphs. Ask what Kiran and Tomás did between the blurry practice and the show, and who did each thing.
support.frame: Kiran felt ______ at first because ______. Later she felt ______ because ______.
support.model:
Mentor example (a different story). A girl feels nervous before a spelling bee. She practices her words with her sister every night. On the day of the bee she feels calm because she practiced. The cause of the change is what she did, not luck.

Now explain the cause of Kiran’s changed feelings in the same way.

misconceptions.d: thinks the adult solved the problem

facts: A shadow’s edges look sharper when the object is close to the screen.
A shadow gets bigger when the light moves closer to the object.

items.stem: Choose the best word for each blank to tell how the characters felt.

dropdown.template: At first, Kiran felt {1} because the shadow looked like a blurry blob. Tomás wanted to {2}. At the end, Kiran felt {3} because the class clapped.

items.explanation: Kiran’s tight stomach and whisper show she was worried. Tomás suggested drawing a picture instead, which means he wanted to give up. The clapping makes her proud.

support.clue: Find what Kiran whispered and what Tomás said after the first practice. Then read the last paragraph to see how Kiran felt after the show.
support.model:
Mentor example (a different story). A boy waits at the nurse’s office with a loose tooth. He feels nervous because he thinks it might hurt. When the tooth comes out, he feels happy because it did not hurt. A feeling word must match what happens.

Now choose feeling words that match what happens in your story.

items.stem: Each group is one change to the shadow. Sort the four sentences so that each action is with the result it caused.

tokens.text: Tomás carried the bird closer to the sheet.
The edges of the shadow became sharp.
Kiran moved the lamp closer to the bird.
The shadow grew bigger and filled the sheet.

items.explanation: Moving the bird closer to the sheet made the edges sharp. Moving the lamp closer to the bird made the shadow bigger. Each action goes with its own result.

support.clue: Reread the fourth paragraph. For each change to the shadow, find what a child did and what happened right after.
support.model:
Mentor example (a different topic). “Mara stirred the paint, so the color became smooth. Then she added water, so the paint became thinner.” Each action goes with the result that follows it.

Now put each action in your story with the result it caused.

facts: A shadow’s edges look sharper when the object is close to the screen.
A shadow gets bigger when the light moves closer to the object.

items.stem: Which two details show that Ms. Okafor wants Kiran and Tomás to solve the problem themselves?

options.text: She asks where the bird is and how far it is from the sheet.
She takes the stick and moves the bird to the right place herself.
She tells them to try a different place and see what changes.
She says the shadow already looks perfect, so they can stop testing.

distractors.b: The story says Ms. Okafor did not take the stick.
distractors.d: Kiran says the shadow does not look right, and Ms. Okafor never says it is perfect.

items.explanation: Asking questions and suggesting a test let the students find the fix on their own.

support.clue: Reread the paragraph where Kiran asks for help. Find the two things Ms. Okafor says, and notice that she does not touch the puppet.
support.frame: Ms. Okafor helps by ______, and she also ______.
support.model:
Mentor example (a different scene). A coach wants a swimmer to fix her own mistake. She asks, “Where are your hands when you kick?” and says, “Try again and watch what changes.” These are two ways to help without doing the work.

Now find two details in your story that work the same way.

misconceptions.b: thinks the adult did the work
misconceptions.d: invents a detail not in the story

items.stem: Kiran says, “Excuse me, could you help us?” Why does she begin with “Excuse me”?

options.text: She wants to speak politely when she asks the teacher for help.
She wants the teacher to leave the hallway so they can practice alone.
She is angry that the teacher walked past without stopping to look.
She wants Tomás to stop talking so that she can ask the question.

distractors.b: Kiran asks for help, so she wants the teacher to stay and listen.
distractors.c: Kiran does not sound angry; she asks a polite question.
distractors.d: Kiran is speaking to Ms. Okafor, and Tomás is not talking at this moment.

items.explanation: “Excuse me” is a polite way to get a teacher’s attention before asking for help.

support.clue: Look at the exact words Kiran uses in the third paragraph. Think about when people say “Excuse me” at school.
support.frame: Kiran says “______” to show she is being ______ when she asks for ______.
support.model:
Mentor example (a different scene). A boy in the lunch line says, “Pardon me, may I get past you?” His opening words tell the other student how he feels toward her. Opening words can show the speaker’s tone.

Now explain the tone of Kiran’s opening words in the same way.

misconceptions.b: misreads the purpose of the phrase

items.stem: Use the schedule. Match each time with what students bring.
items.explanation: The schedule lists a name tag at 9:00, a reading folder at 9:20, and the drawing at 10:15. A lunch box is not on the schedule.

support.clue: Find each time in the first column, then slide your finger across the row to the last column.
support.model:
Mentor example (a different schedule). In a swim-class table, the 4:00 row says “Bring your goggles” and the 4:30 row says “Bring your towel.” To answer, find the time first and then read across to the last column.

Now read across each row of the buddies schedule the same way.

items.stem: Use the schedule to finish the plan. Choose the best word for each blank.

dropdown.template: Students choose a book {1} they go to the library. They go to the art room {2} reading together. At 10:15, they {3} their drawings with the class.

items.explanation: The schedule shows choosing a book at 9:00, before the 9:20 library time. The art room comes at 9:50, after reading. At 10:15 students share drawings.

support.clue: Read the Time column from top to bottom. For each blank, ask which activity comes earlier and which comes later.
support.model:
Mentor example (a different schedule). A bakery plan says: 6:00 mix the dough, 7:00 bake the bread, 8:00 open the doors. We mix the dough before we bake, and we open the doors after the bread is baked.

Now use time words to tell the order of the buddies schedule.
